Having taken the form of a horse, he had intercourse with Philyra, daughter of Oceanus, and for this reason Chiron was born a horse-centaur. His wife was Chariclo. It is reasonable that he introduced an image of Chiron, both because he was the most humane and most just of the Centaurs, and because of his close relationship with Jason; for from him Jason learned the art of medicine, whence he was also called Jason, from 'healing' (iasis).
557. 〈ἐπωλένιον φορέουσα:〉 having it on her arm. Lg

558. Peleus' son Achilles: Apollonius followed the poets after Homer in saying that Achilles was raised by Chiron. But some have disagreed also about the mother of Achilles, as Lysimachus of Alexandria in the second book of the Returns (fg 11 M. III 338), saying verbatim: 'For Souidas (fg 6 M. II 465) and Aristotle, who wrote about Euboea (M. II 142), and the writer of the Phrygian tales (cf. 595 B 299e Diels) and Daïmachus (65 fg 2 J.) and Dionysius of Chalcis (fg 6 M. IV 394) have not left the scattered opinion about Achilles to remain in place, but on the contrary some believe he was born from Thetis, daughter of Chiron, while Daïmachus (see above) says from Philomela, daughter of Actor.'
